sentences.en: This was the diet which bred that hearty race of mortals who won the fields of Cressy and Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 正是这种饮食，孕育了那群在克雷西和阿金库尔战场上所向披靡的英勇之士。

sentences.en: The renowned King Arthur is generally looked upon as the first who ever sat down to a whole roasted ox, which was certainly the best way to preserve the gravy.
sentences.zh: 大名鼎鼎的亚瑟王通常被认为是第一个坐下来享用整只烤牛的人，这无疑是保留肉汁的最佳方式。

sentences.en: And it is further added that he and his knights sat about it at his round table and usually consumed it to the very bones before they would enter on any debate of moment.
sentences.zh: 此外还补充说，他和他的骑士们围坐在圆桌旁，通常在进行任何重要辩论之前，都会把肉吃得连骨头都不剩。

sentences.en: The Black Prince was a professed lover of the brisket, not to mention the history of the sirloin or the institution of the Order of Beef Eaters,
sentences.zh: 黑太子爱德华是牛胸肉的忠实拥趸，更不用说沙朗牛排的历史，或是英国皇家卫队的起源了，

sentences.en: which are all so many evident and undeniable marks of the great respect which our warlike predecessors have paid to this excellent food.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们好战的先辈们对这种绝佳食物怀有崇高敬意的明显且不可否认的标志。

sentences.en: The tables of the ancient gentry of this nation were covered thrice a day with hot roast beef.
sentences.zh: 这个国家古代绅士的餐桌上，每天三次摆满热气腾腾的烤牛肉。

sentences.en: And I am credibly informed by an antiquary who has searched the registers in which the Bill's Affair of the Quarter recorded that instead of tea and bread and butter,
sentences.zh: 一位查阅过季度账单记录的古物研究家曾向我可靠地透露，与现在流行的茶配黄油面包不同，

sentences.en: which have prevailed of late years, the maids of honour in Queen Elizabeth's time were allowed three rumps of beef for their breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白女王时代的宫廷侍女们早餐可以享用三块牛臀肉。

sentences.en: Now that, Dominic, as you will well know because you sent that quote to me, was Joseph Addison writing in the Tatler in 1710 about roast beef.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，正如你所知，因为那段引文是你发给我的，那是约瑟夫·艾迪生1710年在《闲谈者》杂志中关于烤牛肉的描写。

sentences.en: And today we are looking at England, our own native land.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要探讨的是英格兰，我们自己的故土。

sentences.en: And you have chosen as your theme this great theme of roast beef and the role that it's played in notions of liberty and distinctiveness and John Bull and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你选择的主题是烤牛肉，以及它在自由观念、民族独特性、约翰牛形象以及诸如此类的事物中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, England, Tom, I mean, so much to choose from because, of course, we are both English.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，英格兰有太多东西可以讲了，毕竟我们俩都是英国人。

sentences.en: But I thought, why not choose one of the most English things of all, which is roast beef or, indeed, beef and liberty?
sentences.zh: 但我心想，为什么不选一个最具英伦特色的事物呢，那就是烤牛肉，或者说，牛肉与自由？

sentences.en: That's the theme of today's podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天播客的主题。

sentences.en: Now, of course, for you, this is slightly, it's ambiguous ground, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 当然，对你来说，这话题有点微妙，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because while I'm sure you would style yourself a very patriotic Englishman, you are not, it's fair to say, one of life's great beef eaters.
sentences.zh: 因为虽然我相信你会自诩为一个非常爱国的英国人，但平心而论，你并不是那种特别爱吃牛肉的人。

sentences.en: No, not really.
sentences.zh: 不，确实不是。

sentences.en: As in, not at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，完全没有。

sentences.en: Yeah, not at all.
sentences.zh: 没错，完全没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, listeners can draw their own conclusions about the patriotism or otherwise of Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，听众们可以自行判断汤姆·赫兰德是否爱国。

sentences.en: Well, but I love liberty.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但我热爱自由。

sentences.en: You love liberty.
sentences.zh: 你热爱自由。

sentences.en: So, beef and liberty, that's the slogan that's stamped on the buttons of the waistcoat of the members of the Beefsteak Club.
sentences.zh: 所以，“牛肉与自由”就是印在“牛排俱乐部”成员马甲纽扣上的口号。

sentences.en: It is indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And we should be coming to the Beefsteak Club.
sentences.zh: 而且我们应该去一趟牛排俱乐部。

sentences.en: So, you know, roast beef, today, roast beef, I suppose, competes with fish and chips, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，烤牛肉，如今的烤牛肉，我想，应该能和炸鱼薯条一较高下吧？

sentences.en: And chicken tikka masala as one of the great sort of emblematic national dishes.
sentences.zh: 还有鸡肉马萨拉咖喱，它们都是极具代表性的国民美食。

sentences.en: We probably eat less beef per capita than at any time, I would guess, for centuries, wouldn't you say?
sentences.zh: 我猜我们的人均牛肉消费量大概是几个世纪以来的最低水平了，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Because there's so much suspicion of red meat now for health reasons and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为现在出于健康等各种原因，人们对红肉有很多顾虑。

sentences.en: And also, of course, mad cow disease, I'm sure, delivered quite a fatal blow.
sentences.zh: 当然，疯牛病肯定也造成了致命的打击。

sentences.en: I think it did deliver it a blow.
sentences.zh: 我想确实造成了打击。

sentences.en: But the idea of the English as beef eating, so the French, of course, call us les roast beef.
sentences.zh: 但英国人爱吃牛肉的形象，法国人当然就叫我们“烤牛肉佬”。

sentences.en: So, it's not purely our self-image.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不仅仅是我们自己的自我认知。

sentences.en: It's also the way we are perceived.
sentences.zh: 这也是外界对我们的看法。

sentences.en: As we call them, grand oui.
sentences.zh: 就像我们称呼他们那样，法国佬。

sentences.en: Yeah, as we call them frogs.
sentences.zh: 没错，就像我们称呼他们为“青蛙”一样。

sentences.en: And we should be coming to frogs and the contrast between frogs and roast beef in a second.
sentences.zh: 我们马上就会谈到“青蛙”，以及“青蛙”与烤牛肉之间的对比。

sentences.en: But the association between the English, in particular, and beef is an old one.
sentences.zh: 但英国人与牛肉之间的联系由来已久。

sentences.en: So, in Shakespeare's Henry V, which I think is commonly agreed to have been written in 1599, there's a scene just before the Battle of Agincourt.
sentences.zh: 在莎士比亚的《亨利五世》中——我认为普遍认为该剧写于1599年——阿金库尔战役前有一场戏。

sentences.en: And the French are talking.
sentences.zh: 法国人在交谈。

sentences.en: You know, the Constable of France and various other sort of knights and commanders are talking.
sentences.zh: 你知道，法国王室统帅和其他各种骑士、指挥官们正在谈话。

sentences.en: And one Frenchman says, that island of England breeds very valiant creatures.
sentences.zh: 其中一个法国人说，英格兰那个岛屿孕育了非常英勇的生物。

sentences.en: Their mastiffs are of unmatchable courage.
sentences.zh: 他们的獒犬有着无与伦比的勇气。

sentences.en: And the Constable of France says, the men do sympathize with the mastiffs in robustness and rough coming on, leaving their wits with their wives.
sentences.zh: 法国统帅说，这些人就像獒犬一样，身体强壮、冲锋凶猛，却把智慧留给了妻子。

sentences.en: And then give them great meals of beef and iron and steel.
sentences.zh: 然后给他们喂上大量的牛肉、铁和钢。

sentences.en: They will eat like wolves and fight like devils.
sentences.zh: 他们会像狼一样进食，像恶魔一样战斗。

sentences.en: So, even there, at the end of the 16th century, you have a hint of some themes that will become very familiar in this episode.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使在16世纪末，你也能从中窥见一些在本集中会变得非常熟悉的主题。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 那么，

sentences.en: the association of the English with beef and with mastiffs or bulldogs and with bulls and with fighting like animals and with this sort of primitive animal spirits and lack of sophistication.
sentences.zh: 英国人与牛肉、獒犬或斗牛犬、公牛的联系，以及像动物一样战斗、那种原始的动物精神和缺乏教养的特质。

sentences.en: Now, this, of course, is Shakespeare talking.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是莎士比亚在说话。

sentences.en: It's not the French talking.
sentences.zh: 并不是法国人在说话。

sentences.en: And why would beef seem to matter?
sentences.zh: 为什么牛肉显得如此重要呢？

sentences.en: So, well, an obvious reason, Tom, even though you don't eat beef, is that in Tudor England, a lot of people did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，汤姆，一个显而易见的原因是——尽管你不吃牛肉——但在都铎王朝时期的英格兰，很多人都吃。

sentences.en: So, obviously, people let beef all over Europe.
sentences.zh: 显然，整个欧洲的人都吃牛肉。

sentences.en: But I think it's pretty fair to say that the Tudors eat more meat than their neighbours do.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以公平地说，都铎王朝时期的人比他们的邻居吃更多的肉。

sentences.en: Tudor Englishmen and women.
sentences.zh: 都铎王朝时期的英国男女。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, so there's a brilliant book on this, which I should have flagged up already, actually, called Beef and Liberty by a chap called Ben Rogers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一本关于这个主题的精彩著作，我其实早就该提到了，书名叫《牛肉与自由》，作者是一位叫本·罗杰斯的人。

sentences.en: It was published about 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它大约在20年前出版。

sentences.en: An absolutely wonderful journey through this topic from which I have stolen mercilessly balance and poems and so on.
sentences.zh: 这是一段关于该主题的绝妙旅程，我从中毫不客气地借鉴了其中的平衡观点和诗歌等等。

sentences.en: And he says...
sentences.zh: 他说……

sentences.en: But he's speaking to you, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但他是在跟你说话，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the image is...
sentences.zh: 因为那个形象是……

sentences.en: Well, I suppose John Bull.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想是约翰牛。

sentences.en: Well, we'll come to John Bull.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们稍后会谈到约翰牛。

sentences.en: Because John Bull is literally...
sentences.zh: 因为约翰牛字面上……

sentences.en: I mean, he begins as a bull, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他最初是一头公牛，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, I'm not sure whether he does...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不确定他是否是……

sentences.en: There is an association between the English and bulls.
sentences.zh: 英国人和公牛之间确实存在某种联系。

sentences.en: I think John Bull...
sentences.zh: 我认为约翰牛……

sentences.en: Well, we'll come to John Bull.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们稍后会谈到约翰牛。

sentences.en: I shall...
sentences.zh: 我会……

sentences.en: With his waistcoat and his...
sentences.zh: 穿着他的马甲，还有他的……

sentences.en: Yes, okay.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 对不起。

sentences.en: And his pewter tankard and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 还有他的锡制大酒杯，以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: But it's the embodiment of non-metropolitan.
sentences.zh: 但它正是非大都市风格的化身。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Solid...
sentences.zh: 靠谱……

sentences.en: The solid sense of the English gentleman, country gentleman.
sentences.zh: 英国绅士，乡村绅士那扎实的常识。

sentences.en: His waistcoat straining as he devours yet another haunch of beef.
sentences.zh: 他的马甲紧绷着，正狼吞虎咽地吃着又一块牛腿肉。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's pretty much...
sentences.zh: 没错，差不多就是这样……

sentences.en: Solid common sense.
sentences.zh: 非常有道理。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Outraged of chipping Norton.
sentences.zh: 奇平诺顿的愤怒民众。

sentences.en: It's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 可以这么说。

sentences.en: Well, not even outraged, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 嗯，或许称不上愤怒。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我是说……

sentences.en: No, it's phlegmatic.
sentences.zh: 不，那是冷静沉着。

sentences.en: Phlegmatic.
sentences.zh: 冷静沉着。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Phlegmatic.
sentences.zh: 冷漠。

sentences.en: You know, hysterical overreaction.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，歇斯底里的过度反应。

sentences.en: That's the kind of thing that Frenchmen and Londoners get up to.
sentences.zh: 那是法国人和伦敦人会干出的事。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The enthusiasm of all kinds, I think, Tom, is the end.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为各种形式的热情都是终结。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Episcene.
sentences.zh: 柔弱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I've got some great quotes coming about Londoners and their metropolitan foppish ways, which you will be delighted by.
sentences.zh: 我收集了一些关于伦敦人及其大都市浮夸作风的精彩语录，你会喜欢的。

sentences.en: Excellent.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So Ben Rogers, in his book, he says there are obvious reasons why people would eat more beef.
sentences.zh: 所以本·罗杰斯在他的书中提到，人们吃更多牛肉是有显而易见的原因的。

sentences.en: As we've talked about many times, going back to our Anglo-Saxon podcasts, England is very rich in farmland compared with a lot of European countries.
sentences.zh: 正如我们多次讨论过的那样，回顾我们的盎格鲁-撒克逊播客，与许多欧洲国家相比，英格兰拥有非常丰富的农田。

sentences.en: You know, it's got lots of lowlands, green verdant lowlands.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它有很多低地，绿意盎然的低地。

sentences.en: It's perfect for dairy farming.
sentences.zh: 这非常适合奶牛养殖。

sentences.en: It is producing a lot of kind of milk and butter and beef.
sentences.zh: 它出产大量的牛奶、黄油和牛肉。

sentences.en: Over the course of the 16th century, although there are general price rises, so it's a time of great inflation then as now, the price of beef falls relative to other products.
sentences.zh: 在16世纪期间，尽管物价普遍上涨，就像现在一样，那是一个通货膨胀严重的时期，但牛肉的价格相对于其他产品而言却在下降。

sentences.en: So beef is much more readily available.
sentences.zh: 所以牛肉变得更容易买到了。

sentences.en: And one way we can tell how much people ate and how distinctive this was is from travellers' stories.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过旅行者的故事来了解人们吃了多少牛肉，以及这有多么独特。

sentences.en: So first of all, English travellers who go abroad.
sentences.zh: 首先，说说那些去国外的英国旅行者。

sentences.en: So Ben Rogers gives a brilliant example of a chap called Sir Richard Morrison, who goes to Venice in the 1570s.
sentences.zh: 本·罗杰斯举了一个绝佳的例子，讲的是一位叫理查德·莫里森爵士的人，他在16世纪70年代去了威尼斯。

sentences.en: And he says he is astounded by the food.
sentences.zh: 他说他被那里的食物惊呆了。

sentences.en: And he says there is more meat eaten in two months in London than an entire year in Venice.
sentences.zh: 他说伦敦两个月吃的肉比威尼斯一年吃的还要多。

sentences.en: So he's struck.
sentences.zh: 所以他感到很震惊。

sentences.en: Well, not many cows in Venice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，威尼斯没多少牛。

sentences.en: Not many cows, exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实没多少牛。

sentences.en: But also there are other, so there's another, there's an Italian traveller called Alessandro
sentences.zh: 但还有其他的，比如有另一位意大利旅行者叫亚历山德罗·马尼奥，

sentences.en: Magno who comes to London at about the same time.
sentences.zh: 他大约在同一时期来到伦敦。

sentences.en: And he writes in Italian, I assume, it's extraordinary to see the great quantity and quality of meat, beef and mutton that comes every day from the slaughterhouses in the city.
sentences.zh: 我想他是用意大利语写的，他说看到每天从城里屠宰场运出来的牛肉和羊肉数量之大、质量之高，真是非同寻常。

sentences.en: The beef is not expensive and they roast it whole in large pieces.
sentences.zh: 牛肉并不贵，他们把整块肉烤着吃。

sentences.en: For those who cannot see it, it's almost impossible to believe that they could eat so much meat in one city alone.
sentences.zh: 对于没见过的人来说，简直难以相信仅在一个城市就能吃掉这么多肉。

sentences.en: And as time goes on, I think over the next, let's say, 150 years, beef becomes steadily cheaper relative to other meats, partly because of enclosures.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，我想在接下来的150年里，相对于其他肉类，牛肉变得越来越便宜，部分原因是圈地运动。

sentences.en: So farmland is becoming much more productive.
sentences.zh: 所以农田的生产力大大提高了。

sentences.en: So there's just more meat, more butter, more of this sort of stuff being produced.
sentences.zh: 因此，生产出的肉、黄油以及这类东西就更多了。

sentences.en: And also there's the agrarian revolution.
sentences.zh: 而且还有农业革命。

sentences.en: Exactly, the agrarian revolution.
sentences.zh: 没错，农业革命。

sentences.en: Yeah, the town's end and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 是的，圈地运动之类的东西。

sentences.en: So there's just a sort of sense that, you know, there's just more of it and probably better quality.
sentences.zh: 所以人们有一种感觉，就是东西变多了，质量可能也更好了。

sentences.en: And travellers from abroad remark on it more and more as time goes on.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，来自国外的旅行者对此的评价也越来越多。

sentences.en: So in 1698, a Frenchman called Henri Misson, he says at that point, as early as 1698, it
sentences.zh: 1698年，一位叫亨利·米森的法国人说，早在1698年，

sentences.en: is common practice to have a huge piece of roast beef on Sundays of which people stuff until they can swallow no more and they eat the rest cold the other six days of the week.
sentences.zh: 周日吃一大块烤牛肉已是惯例，人们吃到撑不下为止，剩下的部分在接下来六天里冷着吃。

sentences.en: Now, of course, he could have been writing that as late as the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 当然，他这话写在20世纪50年代也不违和。

sentences.en: But he's writing that in the 1690s.
sentences.zh: 但他写于17世纪90年代。

sentences.en: Is there a kind of an association on the part of foreign observers between the eating of beef and the sense of the English as simultaneously violent and phlegmatic?
sentences.zh: 外国观察家是否将英国人吃牛肉与他们既暴力又冷漠的印象联系在一起了呢？

sentences.en: Which seems to be a kind of an abiding theme.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个长久以来的主题。

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: Well, I don't think they make a direct association, but it's absolutely right that the same travellers will be making those points.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为他们有直接的联系，但同样是这些旅行者提出这些观点，这一点是绝对正确的。

sentences.en: So you're absolutely right that the English are perceived as being very violent, disputatious, and yet at the same time gruff and stoical and all these sort of things.
sentences.zh: 所以你说得完全对，英国人被认为非常暴力、好争辩，但同时又显得粗鲁、坚忍，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Like bulls or oxen, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许就像公牛或阉牛一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: So you can sort of see why people would make that, the sort of red-bloodedness, if you like.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以理解为什么人们会产生这种联想，如果你愿意的话，可以称之为热血。

sentences.en: And the converse is that presumably when the English go, say, to France, and they see them all eating frogs and vegetables and onions and things, they think it's very poor.
sentences.zh: 反过来说，大概当英国人去法国时，看到他们都在吃青蛙、蔬菜和洋葱之类的东西，他们会觉得那很寒酸。

sentences.en: And I suppose the archetype of that is William Hogarth's painting.
sentences.zh: 我想威廉·贺加斯的画就是这种典型的代表。

sentences.en: Well, we should come to Hogarth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们应该谈谈贺加斯。

sentences.en: He will play a key part.
sentences.zh: 他将扮演关键角色。

sentences.en: Okay, sorry.
sentences.zh: 好的，抱歉。

sentences.en: So I'm jumping the gun again.
sentences.zh: 看来我又操之过急了。

sentences.en: That's fine, Tom.
sentences.zh: 没关系，汤姆。

sentences.en: It's good to anticipate.
sentences.zh: 有预见性是好事。

sentences.en: Slaking it up.
sentences.zh: 大快朵颐。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So the English are definitely eating an awful lot of beef.
sentences.zh: 所以英国人确实吃掉大量的牛肉。

sentences.en: Ben Rogers calls us the Texans of the early modern world.
sentences.zh: 本·罗杰斯称我们为近代早期的德克萨斯人。

sentences.en: And I think that's a, for our Texan listeners, that's a comparison I welcome.
sentences.zh: 我想对于我们的德克萨斯听众来说，这是一个我乐于接受的比较。

sentences.en: If it's associated with any one class in particular, he thinks it's associated with yeoman.
sentences.zh: 如果说它与某个特定阶层有关，他认为那应该是自耕农。

sentences.en: So yeoman farmers.
sentences.zh: 也就是自耕农。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're not the gentry.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以你们不是乡绅阶层。

sentences.en: Well, the gentry will eat beef.
sentences.zh: 嗯，乡绅也会吃牛肉。

sentences.en: And in fact, some of these travellers do remark on this.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些旅行者确实注意到了这一点。

sentences.en: A Swiss traveller in 1726 called Monsieur Mural, he says, they'll eat roast beef as well at a king's table as at a tradesman's.
sentences.zh: 一位1726年的瑞士旅行者穆拉尔先生说，他们吃烤牛肉，无论是国王的餐桌还是商人的餐桌上都有。

sentences.en: So there's actually an odd sense in which the eating of roast beef is, is it democratic?
sentences.zh: 所以，吃烤牛肉在某种奇怪的意义上，难道是民主的吗？

sentences.en: That's probably the wrong word.
sentences.zh: 这可能用词不当。

sentences.en: But it's universal.
sentences.zh: 但它是普遍的。

sentences.en: But also an index of wealth, presumably.
sentences.zh: 但想必也是财富的象征。

sentences.en: Yes, although it's not that expensive.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管它并不那么昂贵。

sentences.en: Again, the point is it's not that expensive.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，重点是它并不那么贵。

sentences.en: So if you're eating stuffed quails or something, then you're rich.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你吃的是酿鹌鹑之类的东西，那你才是有钱人。

sentences.en: But presumably it's quite expensive on the continent relative to the expensive in England.
sentences.zh: 但想必相对于英国的物价，它在欧洲大陆应该相当昂贵吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我想这绝对正确。

sentences.en: I think it's because England has still this farmland or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为英国仍然拥有这些农田之类的资源。

sentences.en: I'm not a massive agrarian specialist, it's fair to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 说实话，汤姆，我不是什么农业专家。

sentences.en: It's up there with my knowledge of Portuguese sailing technology.
sentences.zh: 这和我在葡萄牙航海技术方面的知识水平差不多。

sentences.en: But because we have all this, beef is readily available.
sentences.zh: 但因为我们拥有这一切，牛肉很容易获得。

sentences.en: Slaughterhouses pumping out all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 屠宰场源源不断地生产这些东西。

sentences.en: If slaughterhouses can.
sentences.zh: 如果屠宰场能做到的话。

sentences.en: I mean, the stuff they're pumping out, actually, I don't even want to think about.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们生产的那些东西，其实我连想都不敢想。

sentences.en: I think that's sausage factories.
sentences.zh: 我想那是香肠工厂。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Food manufacturers.
sentences.zh: 食品制造商。

sentences.en: But it's associated with yeoman farmers.
sentences.zh: 但它与自耕农有关。

sentences.en: And of course, the yeoman of the guard are known as beef eaters.
sentences.zh: 当然，御林军也被称为“吃牛肉的人”。

sentences.en: Of course they are, yes.
sentences.zh: 他们当然是，没错。

sentences.en: And how long does that go back?
sentences.zh: 那这个称呼由来已久了吗？

sentences.en: How far does that go back?
sentences.zh: 这可以追溯到多久以前？

sentences.en: Well, I think that that goes back centuries, actually.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这实际上可以追溯到几个世纪前。

sentences.en: There are various explanations about why they're called beef eaters.
sentences.zh: 关于他们为什么被称为“吃牛肉的人”，有各种各样的解释。

sentences.en: But Rogers points out that right up to the 19th century, if you're a yeoman of the guard, you are given a ration of beef every day.
sentences.zh: 但罗杰斯指出，直到19世纪，如果你是御林军，你每天都会得到一份牛肉配给。

sentences.en: So if you're a yeoman of the guard at St. James's Palace, you are still being given 24 pounds of beef a day, which is a lot of beef.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是圣詹姆斯宫的御林军，你每天仍然会得到24磅牛肉，这可是相当多的牛肉。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, here's a key thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，关键点来了。

sentences.en: How do people cook it?
sentences.zh: 人们是怎么烹饪它的呢？

sentences.en: You might think this is a bit abstruse, but actually this comes back to this point about liberty, and we'll get to it.
sentences.zh: 你可能觉得这有点深奥，但实际上这又回到了关于自由的那个观点，我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: I'll explain why.
sentences.zh: 我会解释原因。

sentences.en: Not with garlic.
sentences.zh: 不是用大蒜。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: If you're in Italy or in France, the way they have their meat in the early modern period is they will often fry it or braise it or stew it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在意大利或法国，在近代早期，他们吃肉的方式通常是煎、焖或炖。

sentences.en: The English like to roast it.
sentences.zh: 英国人喜欢烤着吃。

sentences.en: And what they – now, I didn't know this, actually.
sentences.zh: 而他们——我以前真不知道这一点。

sentences.en: I find this fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太迷人了。

sentences.en: The word roast and rotate have the same kind of derivation.
sentences.zh: “烤”（roast）和“旋转”（rotate）有着相同的词源。

sentences.en: Roti.
sentences.zh: Roti（烤肉）。

sentences.en: So they're basically the same word.
sentences.zh: 所以它们基本上是同一个词。

sentences.en: And the way you would roast it, you've got an open fire, you put it on a spit, and you rotate it initially by hand.
sentences.zh: 而你烤肉的方式是，你有一个露天火堆，把它放在烤叉上，起初是用手旋转它。

sentences.en: But over time – I mean, that's very time-consuming and boring.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移——我是说，那非常耗时且无聊。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you need a scullion.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且你需要一个厨房杂役。

sentences.en: What if you don't have a scullion?
sentences.zh: 如果你没有厨房杂役怎么办？

sentences.en: You get a dog to do it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你找条狗来做，汤姆。

sentences.en: How do you get a dog to do it?
sentences.zh: 你怎么让狗来做呢？

sentences.en: So they basically trap a dog on a treadmill.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是把狗困在跑步机上。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And the dog revolves the spit.
sentences.zh: 然后狗就转动了烤叉。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Beef or liberty.
sentences.zh: 牛肉还是自由。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, not liberty for dogs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对狗来说可不是自由。

sentences.en: No liberty for the dogs.
sentences.zh: 狗没有自由。

sentences.en: But over time, they develop these things called meat jacks, which are mechanical, and they have weights.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，他们发明了被称为“烤肉机”的东西，它们是机械的，带有重物。

sentences.en: How do they work, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 它们是怎么工作的，多米尼克？

sentences.en: It's a complicated system of weights, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的重力系统，汤姆。

sentences.en: I know you wouldn't understand.
sentences.zh: 我知道你不会明白的。

sentences.en: Weights going up and down and the thing rotating.
sentences.zh: 重物上下移动，然后东西就旋转起来了。

sentences.en: I think that's a technical explanation.
sentences.zh: 我想那是一个技术性的解释。

sentences.en: Thanks for clearing that up.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的澄清。

sentences.en: So by the – Dr. Johnson, I think, grew up in a home in Litchfield with a meat jack.
sentences.zh: 所以到了——我想约翰逊博士是在利奇菲尔德的一个家里长大的，那里就有烤肉机。

sentences.en: Of course he would.
sentences.zh: 他当然会有。

sentences.en: Dr. Johnson is the physical embodiment of a beef eater.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊博士就是“吃牛肉的人”的化身。

sentences.en: So a Finnish writer called Per Kalm.
sentences.zh: 所以一位名叫佩尔·卡尔姆的芬兰作家。

sentences.en: He visited in the late 18th century, and he said they have meat jacks in every house in England, which was clearly an exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 他在18世纪末访问时说，英国每家每户都有烤肉机，这显然是夸大其词。

sentences.en: But maybe they had them in every house he visited.
sentences.zh: 但也许他拜访的每家每户都有。

sentences.en: I mean, that's perfectly plausible.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这完全说得通。

sentences.en: So roasting meat is absolutely part of the sort of national – it's a national custom, I suppose you can say.
sentences.zh: 所以烤肉绝对是某种民族——我想你可以说是一种民族习俗。

sentences.en: So how do you eat it?
sentences.zh: 那么你怎么吃它呢？

sentences.en: So you've roasted it.
sentences.zh: 你把它烤好了。

sentences.en: You have it in its own juices.
sentences.zh: 你用它自己的肉汁来吃。

sentences.en: You have it in – that's its gravy.
sentences.zh: 你用它——那就是肉汁（gravy）。

sentences.en: You do not have it with a fancy stock or a sauce, which is why Voltaire said the English have 100 different religions, but only one sauce.
sentences.zh: 你不会用精致的高汤或酱汁来吃，这就是为什么伏尔泰说英国有一百种宗教，却只有一种酱汁。

sentences.en: And this is the sauce, you see.
sentences.zh: 而这就是那种酱汁，你看。

sentences.en: So you don't have any fancy sauce.
sentences.zh: 所以你没有任何精致的酱汁。

sentences.en: You have it with this gravy.
sentences.zh: 你用这种肉汁吃。

sentences.en: You have it with condiments.
sentences.zh: 你配着调味品吃。

sentences.en: So traditionally, English mustard – I don't really know why.
sentences.zh: 所以传统上是英式芥末——我真的不知道为什么。

sentences.en: Possibly, I guess, lack of access to spices, but English mustard had always been stronger than continental.
sentences.zh: 可能吧，我猜是因为缺乏香料，但英式芥末一直比欧洲大陆的更浓烈。

sentences.en: Well, surely that reflects our love of liberty.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这肯定反映了我们对自由的热爱。

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: We're just strong people, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我们只是坚强的人，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's just no Frenchified nonsense about our mustard.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的芥末里没有那种法式的胡闹。

sentences.en: So in England, mustard was mixed with horseradish to make it stronger, and horseradish itself was mixed with vinegar.
sentences.zh: 所以在英国，芥末与辣根混合以使其更浓烈，而辣根本身则与醋混合。

sentences.en: In France, they mixed it with cream, which made it more mellow, mild.
sentences.zh: 在法国，他们把它与奶油混合，这使它更柔和、温和。

sentences.en: Typical.
sentences.zh: 典型。

sentences.en: But in England, people mixed it with vinegar.
sentences.zh: 但在英国，人们把它与醋混合。

sentences.en: So these continental travellers who are tucking into their beef are kind of –
sentences.zh: 所以这些正在大快朵颐牛肉的欧洲大陆旅行者有点——

sentences.en: Whoa!
sentences.zh: 哇！

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Sort of sobbing with agony as they eat their horseradish and mustard.
sentences.zh: 吃着辣根和芥末时痛苦得啜泣。

sentences.en: The other thing you would have it with, Tom, are you a big believer in puddings?
sentences.zh: 你还会配着别的东西吃，汤姆，你是个布丁的忠实信徒吗？

sentences.en: I am, yes.
sentences.zh: 我是，是的。

sentences.en: Because this is my father.
sentences.zh: 因为这是我父亲。

sentences.en: What kind of puddings do you like?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢什么样的布丁？

sentences.en: We never go out for a meal, and he will always say, is there any pud?
sentences.zh: 我们从不出去吃饭，他总会问，有布丁吗？

sentences.en: And there always is.
sentences.zh: 而且总是有。

sentences.en: But he would eat that after his main course, am I right?
sentences.zh: 但他会在主菜之后吃，我没说错吧？

sentences.en: Yes, he would, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，他会，没错。

sentences.en: Well, you see, if you were in the 18th century, that would be very strange and outlandish behaviour.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，如果你在18世纪，那将是非常奇怪和古怪的行为。

sentences.en: You would eat your pudding alongside, and it would be a pudding.
sentences.zh: 你会把布丁和主菜一起吃，而且它会是一个布丁。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: So made of suet or something.
sentences.zh: 所以是用牛脂之类的做的。

sentences.en: Or conceivably a pie.
sentences.zh: 或者可以想象成一个馅饼。

sentences.en: And so originally, we in England – I know we have a lot of Australian and American listeners who probably find it weird our terminology for what they would call desserts,
sentences.zh: 所以最初，我们在英国——我知道我们有很多澳大利亚和美国听众，他们可能觉得我们对他们所谓的甜点的称呼很奇怪，

sentences.en: that we call them puddings, even when they're not a pudding.
sentences.zh: 我们称它们为布丁，即使它们根本不是布丁。

sentences.en: Originally, a pudding was a kind of cousin of the sausage.
sentences.zh: 最初，布丁是香肠的一种近亲。

sentences.en: So it was like a sort of skin.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像一种皮。

sentences.en: So steak and kidney pudding.
sentences.zh: 比如牛排腰子布丁。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Ben Rogers says the closest you can come to a pudding is actually eating haggis.
sentences.zh: 本·罗杰斯说，你所能吃到的最接近布丁的东西其实是哈吉斯（羊杂碎布丁）。

sentences.en: Haggis is basically a pudding.
sentences.zh: 哈吉斯基本上就是一种布丁。

sentences.en: So skin stuffed with stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以就是塞满了东西的皮。

sentences.en: And interestingly, at this point, so early modern England, people didn't distinguish between sweet and savoury.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在这一点上，也就是近代早期的英国，人们并不区分甜味和咸味。

sentences.en: And they'd shove the two in together.
sentences.zh: 他们会把两者混在一起吃。

sentences.en: So sweet meats.
sentences.zh: 所以有甜肉。

sentences.en: Well, this explains to me something that has always puzzled me, which is if I say to you, would you like a mince pie?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这向我解释了一件一直让我困惑的事情，那就是如果我对你说，你想来个百果馅饼（mince pie）吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's the sweet one.
sentences.zh: 那是甜的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Or a pudding with mince in it.
sentences.zh: 或者里面有肉馅的布丁。

sentences.en: Go and buy me some mince meat, Tom.
sentences.zh: 去给我买点肉馅（mince meat），汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What would you come back with?
sentences.zh: 你会带回来什么？

sentences.en: Will you come back with minced meat or mince meat, which is completely different and is sweet?
sentences.zh: 你会带回来绞碎的肉（minced meat）还是百果馅（mince meat），它们完全不同，后者是甜的？

sentences.en: So Christmas pudding is a kind of the last remnant, one of the last remnants of this world.
sentences.zh: 所以圣诞布丁是这个世界的一种最后遗迹，最后的遗迹之一。

sentences.en: It's a plum pudding, but people would have had puddings where they'd have shoved all kinds of stuff in them.
sentences.zh: 它是李子布丁，但人们过去吃的布丁里会塞进各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, this is an astonishing diet then.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那时的饮食真是令人震惊。

sentences.en: So you're having your roast beef and then you're having a meat pudding at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以你吃着烤牛肉，同时又吃着肉布丁。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, no wonder we're rushing around conquering the world with all that amount of meat.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难怪我们吃那么多肉，还能到处征服世界。

sentences.en: And you're washing this down, not with French wines, but with ale or porter or fortified wine port.
sentences.zh: 而且你们不是用法国葡萄酒，而是用艾尔啤酒、波特啤酒或波特加强型葡萄酒来佐餐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, from Portugal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是来自葡萄牙的那种。

sentences.en: From our oldest ally.
sentences.zh: 来自我们最古老的盟友。

sentences.en: So it's fair to say it's quite heavy.
sentences.zh: 所以说这种饮食相当油腻是很中肯的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's quite a heavy diet.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一种很油腻的饮食。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, gout must be a constant risk.
sentences.zh: 我是说，痛风肯定是个持续存在的风险。

sentences.en: Well, this is, I mean, who was it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个，我是说，那是谁来着？

sentences.en: Who was a three-bottle man?
sentences.zh: 谁是那种“三瓶酒男人”？

sentences.en: Was it William Pitt the Younger that we were talking about in our Prime Minister's podcast?
sentences.zh: 我们在首相播客里谈论的是小威廉·皮特吗？

sentences.en: So three bottles, puddings, beef.
sentences.zh: 所以是三瓶酒、布丁、牛肉。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a great diet.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真是绝佳的饮食。

sentences.en: It's amazing that people live beyond the age of 40.
sentences.zh: 人们能活过40岁真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: And again, I hope I'm not jumping the gun.
